## Design

### 2026-10-07 – This is a  entry I started yesterday. First I worked on researching parts for what to make this creation out of. Originally I wanted to use a bigger 1.8 inch rgb display but for this it won’t be neede

**2h**

This is a  entry I started yesterday. First I worked on researching parts for what to make this creation out of. Originally I wanted to use a bigger 1.8 inch rgb display but for this it won’t be needed so I decided to stick with a 0.96 oled one.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/B7DyTHWMKLlVBPhtAoOx01uK0x4UwPcR/3c6ca3213f5360fc693f8d5871ff38c122084b07d0cb9e61d62645712e9a0b97.jpg)
-0.96 oled screen

I researched sensors after this and I originally wanted to do a DHT11 sensor.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/B7DyTHWMKLlVBPhtAoOx01uK0x4UwPcR/86fedf8d88de4df9c48d9f5b85101e25a7cc19b5edc02468287019843cd74357.jpg)
-inferior DHT11 sensor that I have already

 I have used this sensor before but I decided to go with a AHT20 sensor. This new sensor is much more accurate than the previous one so it would also require less calibration if needed. A downside is that the AHT20 sensor requires one more data pin than the DHT11 so the whole pcb would be a little more complicated but that is a small downside at best. I also would be using the esp32 wroom module to be the brains of the pcb. For the buzzer I decided on the b814 buzzer or another piezo electric buzzer would be the best as they are the loudest.

After this i will work on a mock up breadboard version of this with the parts that i have.

### 2026-10-07 – The first thing i did was wire up the mock up with the parts i had.

**3.23h**

The first thing i did was wire up the mock up with the parts i had.
- The bread boards
- Wires
- Esp32 devkit
- .96 oled
- DHT11 sensor
- Power supply module
- Buzzer
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/B7DyTHWMKLlVBPhtAoOx01uK0x4UwPcR/46038bc0c760953a796182452662b4b8a67b1cc891f727be83ab9ea140c28f56.jpg)

This part refreshed my memory a lot about electronics as i haven't touched a project in a while

Coding was the next part,  I managed to get through it but not without major hiccups. For example :

- The software i coded in, arduino ide, is based on c++ so there's some gimmicks i find annoying like having a ; to end every line.
- My laptop died mid way through but thankfully i didn't lose much progress as the code i wrote at that point was very messy and unorganized mostly because i decided not to label or use #define originally
- Simple things like setting the threshold temperature was also a struggle as i didn't know the proper thing to type which ended up being something very simple

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/B7DyTHWMKLlVBPhtAoOx01uK0x4UwPcR/833f9a2b32ac5d9de0aab37041b293c426a03a9893fa0650ba7a858fef3360f1.jpg)

- Issues i had with the actual electronics were the buzzer being constantly on at boot and issues with a dead 9v battery and me realizing that wasn't the issue
- My laptop ended up dying again but i saved the code. Unfortunate it kept randomly shutting off so i had to spend some time trying to fix that which hopefully worked. Very glad the drafts for the entrys save.

![IMG_0119](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/B7DyTHWMKLlVBPhtAoOx01uK0x4UwPcR/30dec7128fffa4f6c33349c7abd77e2b275acb06c54107e94ef160fe8db9ad61.jpg)

After i finally got it to work the only problem that was left was a quiet buzzer. That's most likely due to the buzzer it self. Additionally the temp sensor was very inaccurate shifting 1 degrees pretty quick

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/B7DyTHWMKLlVBPhtAoOx01uK0x4UwPcR/5019377d477cb8029683cd8b86c6d333e2fa583b09e8c06c22e92c1afc416ca0.jpg)
When below 28C (buzzer replaced with led for better representation)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/B7DyTHWMKLlVBPhtAoOx01uK0x4UwPcR/3dd8f9c5f519aed5a354056487ff1dfc2547a6f4d251a5bf4b00f5860e1d46e3.jpg)

When above 28C ( as you can see the led is on and the screen is flashing inverse to normal)

For my next entry i will download ki cad and starting an actual pcb schematic with the proper parts and diagrams.

### 2026-10-10 – Today i downloaded Ki-Cad and started work on the pcb.

**2.62h**

Today i downloaded Ki-Cad and started work on the pcb.

At first i had issues with trying to get kicad to work and also trying to download a esp32 symbols and footprint but it worked in the end. The work i did had a lot of issues with the pcb I'm not sure it will work right now but i think i have all the symbols and footprints.

I also decided to replace the buzzer with a speaker that will play an alarm sound instead as an added challenge. I researched for some time and i think i found a good speaker and amplifier.

Next entry i will try to flush everything out completely and hopefully be done.
